estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Consensual Assessment Technique: ten professional poets rated each poem from one (lowest creativity) to forty (highest creativity), relative to the other poems and using the full scale. Poems were presented in independently randomized orders without information about authors or production conditions (PDF pp. 3-4). Rating aggregation and inter-rater reliability are not reported. The analysis is a one-way ANOVA with post hoc pairwise comparisons; Table 1 identifies LSD tests (PDF p. 4).

estimates.notes: One poem was submitted per randomized person, so the human-arm SDs are participant-level and se_basis is participant under the one-output-per-person rule. unit=output and n_units=146 retain the paper's full ANOVA unit and printed poem count, as in the reconciled form; that count includes the AI-only benchmark, not additional people in this contrast. The post hoc p-value uses the three-group error term, including the 50 AI-only poems (PDF p. 4). No pairwise test statistic, standardized effect, SE, or CI is printed. The omnibus ANOVA and its partial eta-squared are not two-arm statistics. The paper reports 101 recruits, six exclusions, and 96 remaining participants (PDF p. 2); the discrepancy is retained and n_randomized is null because the timing and arm allocation of exclusions are not stated. The printed omnibus error degrees of freedom also conflict with the stated poem count. No numerical effect has been derived.

open_items: Study 1 reports 101 recruits, six attention-check exclusions, and 96 remaining participants (PDF p. 2). These counts are inconsistent. The arm counts of 48 each are printed; the paper does not state exclusion timing or excluded participants' arms, so randomized counts remain null.

Study 1 prints an omnibus error df of 145 while reporting 146 poems in the three-group analysis (PDF p. 4). This inconsistency and the use of AI-only benchmark poems in the post hoc error term remain unresolved; neither omnibus statistics nor a derived pairwise statistic is entered.
Study 2 human-arm expert-creativity SD is 9.24 in the prose (PDF p. 6) and 4.98 in Table 2 (PDF p. 7). The extraction uses the table value and retains the conflict.

Study 2 co-creator versus human expert-creativity comparison explicitly reports p = 0.278, but p = 0.280 also appears after the co-creator descriptive statistics in the same passage (PDF p. 6). The explicit pairwise value is extracted.
Neither study states how individual poets' ratings were aggregated per poem or reports inter-rater reliability (PDF pp. 3-7).

No pairwise creativity SEs, numerical CI bounds, or pairwise test statistics are printed in the text or tables. Figure-only values are not transcribed. Study 2 does not print the people total separately for each pairwise comparison (PDF pp. 4-7).

The editor instructions permitted submitting the supplied AI poem unchanged, but the paper reports no editing-frequency or editing-extent data (PDF p. 3; Study 2 follows the same procedure on PDF p. 5).
notes: Extraction date: 2026-10-10. The complete markdown conversion was read, including Methods, references, and end matter; there are no appendices or supplementary sections in the saved document. Text from every PDF page was extracted with pymupdf, and Tables 1 and 2 were also checked with find_tables(). PDF and printed page numbers agree. Only printed numbers are transcribed; no standardized effects, differences, sample totals, SEs, or intervals were computed. Numeric JSON values retain their values; source quotes preserve printed decimal precision, including trailing zeros. Random individual assignment is explicit in each study description and in Methods (PDF p. 9). Participants were English-first-language adults recruited through Prolific; participant country is not stated (PDF pp. 8-9). Study 1 randomized counts are unknown; Study 2 reports no attention-check failures and its allocation counts are used for both randomized and analyzed counts. The neural generator is within scope under the codebook's explicit inclusion of the Van de Cruys system. The editor role is coded ideas_supplied because the complete supplied draft defines that arm, although responsive AI line suggestions are also available. Study 2 uses ai_role=other because it combines that editor role with the co-creator suggestions role. The paper reports no across-people diversity or after-AI outcome and no combined-AI arm contrast. The screening form reports no shared sample with another paper. OSF is identified as a data-and-syntax repository, not a supplement, and was not used.
